Lag Sequential Analysis Across Several Lags

Source: R/lsa-lags.R
lsa_lags.Rd

Fits lsa() at each requested lag and returns the fits together, so you can compare a transition's strength across lags (a lag profile). Each element is an ordinary lsa fit.

Usage

lsa_lags(data, lags = 1:3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_lags'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_lags'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

data

Sequence input (any form accepted by lsa()).

lags

Integer vector of lags. May include negative lags (predecessors) and 0. Default 1:3.

...

Passed to lsa() (e.g. engine, alpha, structural_zeros). Ignored by the print() and as.data.frame() methods.

x

An lsa_lags object (print() and as.data.frame() methods).

row.names

Optional row names for the stacked data frame.

optional

Ignored; present for consistency with the generic.

Value

An object of class c("lsa_lags", "list"): a named list of lsa fits (names "lag1", "lag2", ...), with a lags attribute. transitions() (with all its filtering arguments) and as.data.frame() row-bind the per-lag transition tables (each carries its lag column) into one tidy frame, one row per transition and lag, with the same columns as transitions(). print() lists the number of significant transitions per lag and returns x invisibly.

See also

lsa()

Examples

prof <- lsa_lags(engagement, lags = 1:3)
prof
#> <lsa_lags>
#>   engine: classical
#>   lags:   1, 2, 3
#>     lag 1    7 of 9 transitions significant
#>     lag 2    8 of 9 transitions significant
#>     lag 3    8 of 9 transitions significant
transitions(prof, significant = TRUE, sort = "strength")

# Track one transition across lags with the dedicated verb:
lag_profile(engagement, from = "Active", to = "Average", lags = 1:3)
